text: Shortage of mechanical and electrical engineers at both degree level and higher technical qualification level.
Qualified electricians are hard to find, and new legal standards from October 2026 mean even more will be needed.
Severe shortage of bricklayers, despite strong housebuilding demand across GM.
Long-standing shortage of qualified quantity surveyors, the hardest role to fill alongside electricians.
Shortage of roofers, with low numbers and quality of applicants for vacancies.
Shortage of Class 1 HGV drivers with 3-5 years' experience, made worse by poor early support for new drivers.
Shortage of business development skills specific to the logistics sector.
Shortage of customer service skills for customer-facing logistics roles.
Severe shortage of healthcare assistants, worsened since Covid by the pull of better-paid agency work.
Not enough nurses to meet demand, especially in nursing and care homes competing with the NHS and agencies.
Low uptake of Level 3-5 senior care qualifications, leaving a shortage of senior and managerial care staff.
Shortage of advanced degree-level (Level 6) engineers, including electrical, mechanical and aerospace engineers.
Labour shortage across core manufacturing trades: production operatives, electronics technicians, mechanical fitters and welders.
Growing need for advanced manufacturing trade skills such as robotics, mechatronics and CNC machining.
An ageing workforce and around 47,000 unfilled engineering vacancies since the EU exit add to the pressure.
Shortage of cybersecurity professionals, both as a labour shortage and a skills gap in existing IT staff.
Rising demand for data roles (data engineers, analysts, product owners) at all levels.
Shortage of cloud computing skills, for example AWS certifications, as more firms move systems online.
Emerging shortage of AI and machine learning engineering skills as employers adopt AI faster than the talent pipeline grows.
IT technicians are in high demand, with a good pipeline for entry-level roles but weaker progression into mid-level and management.
Shortage of AI skills in the creative sector as generative AI changes design, writing and video roles.
Shortages in technical live-performance skills (sound, lighting, hair and make-up) and inefficient use of existing freelance skills.
Growing demand for digital marketing skills as the number of specialisms under 'digital marketing' keeps expanding.
Small but intensifying shortage of augmented reality and virtual reality skills.
Labour shortage of chefs across hotels, restaurants and in-house catering settings.
Mid-level hospitality roles (such as chef de partie) are hard to fill, and junior staff often do not stay to progress.
Shortage of qualified solicitors who have completed the SQE route, especially in property, wills and probate, and corporate law.
Shortage of B2B business development and sales skills across financial and professional services firms.
Shortage of experienced accountancy and finance professionals, including chartered accountants and finance managers.
